terms.gloss: a person; in the plural, people
terms.comment: The plural hominēs is the everyday “people”.
Above all in omnēs mortālēs, everybody.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.28: in forō turbāque (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a people, a nation; the public
terms.comment: The people as a body, not persons: populus Rōmānus. Cicero defines it as nōn omnis hominum coetus quōquō modō congregātus.

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī
phrases.english: every one of us slips up; we’re people, not gods

phrases.latin: ō quantum est hominum beātiōrum, quid mē laetius est beātiusve?
phrases.english: of all the happier people there are, who is gladder or happier than me?

sources: Lewis & Short: homo · Lewis & Short: mortalis · Lewis & Short: turba · Lewis & Short: populus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 178, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
